text:
elaine.cs: FYI customer report — ACME Prod seeing p99 tail jump ~4.2s for text-generation API since ~09:12 UTC, previously ~650ms. They also saw a few 137 OOMs and increased retries. Request id samples: r=acme-req-8001,r=acme-req-8042.

sam.support: on it. Any tenant id / model they hit?

elaine.cs: tenant=acme-inc, model=redwood-xl-8k, mostly streaming generation with avg seq len ~150 tokens but some long-lived sessions with many prefix messages.

raj.oncall: I pulled infra metrics — cluster gpu mem usage creeping, GPU mem util ~92% on node-gpu-12 and nv-pg 0 shows many small allocated chunks. nvml snapshot attached (excerpt):
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 530.41.03    Driver Version: 530.41.03    CUDA Version: 12.1  |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A100-SXM-80GB   On        | 00000000:3D:00.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   PID   Type   Process name                  GPU-Mem |
|    0  12345  C      /usr/bin/inference_runtime     76012MiB|
|    0  12346  C      /usr/bin/inference_runtime     1024MiB|
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

chris.runtime: that pattern (one big process + many tiny allocations) screams slab fragmentation + KV growth. Any recent rollout?

deploy-bot: rollout redwood-xl-8k-v2 -> v3 completed at 09:05 UTC on cluster-prod (canary 10%).

raj.oncall: rollout at 09:05 aligns. perf-bot shows p95 stable but p99 jumped right after canary increased at 09:10. Link: https://perf.redwood/boards/tenants/acme-inc?range=1h (perf-bot)

perf-bot: p50 120ms p95 420ms p99 4.2s — spike concentrated on model-serving pods on node-gpu-12.

sam.support: do we have heap/kv metrics for the runtime? I can ask customer for a short repro but want to triage first.

chris.runtime: ask customer to send a sample session payload that triggers repeated prefix caching. Meanwhile do these quick mitigations in this order:
1) Temporarily enable KV TTL for tenant: `runtimectl set-tenant-config acme-inc --kv-ttl=30m`
2) Reduce max-session-length: `runtimectl set-tenant-config acme-inc --max-prefix-messages=200`
3) Roll runtime pods on node-gpu-12: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime -l node=gpu-12 --namespace=prod` (staggered)
4) If p99 still high, enable slab defrag and reduced allocator frag threshold: `--slab-defrag=true --allocator-max-frag=0.15` (needs controlled rollout).

elaine.cs: I relayed 1+2 to ACME and they allowed a rolling restart. They also provided a redacted session that reproduces the growth (I'll paste in a sec).

raj.oncall: I'll trigger a restart on the affected node and watch mem defrag metrics. Will also capture heap profile via /debug/heap for the runtime process.

chris.runtime: also candidate immediate fallback: route ACME to smaller variant `redwood-large-8k` for traffic > 2s latency to keep them stable while we debug. Can do routing rule for tenant.

sam.support: repro payload from customer below (redacted):
```
POST /v1/chat/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Body: {"messages": [{"role":"system","content":"x"}, {"role":"user","content":"question"}, ... repeated ~300 times], "stream": true}
```

elaine.cs: roll started at 09:28 UTC, node restart done 09:33 UTC (staggered). I asked ACME to resume testing at 09:40.

perf-bot: p99 dropped to 1.1s by 09:48 UTC after restart + KV TTL applied. OOMs stopped. p95 unchanged.

raj.oncall: captured heap profile and KV key-count shows per-tenant growth to ~1.2M keys (long sessions kept writing prefixes). There's a missing TTL enforcement bug for migration path when canary rolled — creating unbounded KV retention. Filing infra bug: INF-6124.

chris.runtime: INF-6124 acknowledged. Immediate follow-ups: a) Hotfix to ensure TTL applied on older kv shards *and* backfill cleanup b) Add tenant-level kv-rate-limiter c) Add defensive eviction when key-count > 200k with LRU. I'll own the hotfix.

elaine.cs: ACME confirmed latency improved and accepted rolling change for now. They asked for a postmortem and ETA on hotfix.

sam.support: action items summarized:
- chris.runtime: patch INF-6124 hotfix + deployment plan (ETA 8h)
- raj.oncall: KV backfill cleanup job + heap trace + watch p99 (in progress)
- support: keep ACME updated, propose fallback routing if recurrence

chris.runtime: starting hotfix branch now. I will also add telemetry for per-tenant kv-key-count and a guard in the allocator that logs fragmentation ratio > 0.6.

elaine.cs: thanks all — closing loop with ACME and will paste their final note when they send it. :thumbsup:
